newsitem.title: USA: GE Capital may expand into property insurance.
newsitem.headline: GE Capital may expand into property insurance.

text.p: GE Capital Assurance, one of the largest US life insurers, may expand into the personal lines property-casualty insurance business, a top GE executive said.
"We may have some interest there," said Victor Moses, senior vice-president for GE Capital's GNA Corp.
"We're exploring it," he said, speaking at the second annual Congress on Mergers, Acquisitions and Financings in the Insurance Industry.
GE Capital, a unit of General Electric Co, has been one of the most active players in the consolidation of the life insurance industry.
However GE Capital currently does not have a U.S. personal lines property-casualty operation, Moses said.
"It's an area we're not in yet but one we have some interest in," he said.
GE Capital expected to close on the acquisition of a small property-casualty business in Mexico in late November.
GE Capital also is exploring other acquisition opportunities in international markets, Moses said.

He said GE Capital has a three-person team in Mexico exploring opportunities and has another three-person team in Europe exploring acquisition opportunities there. He said he expects GE Capital to have a third team in Asia next year to explore acquisition in that region. As for its life insurance business, Moses said GE Capital believes it has all the pieces in place that it needs to be a large and efficient player in the U.S. market.
He said he expects GE to build upon that business primarily through the acquisition of blocks of business.
GE Capital expects to "grow and integrate what we have," he said.
"But that doesn't mean we're going to withdraw entirely (from the merger market)," he said.
The conference was sponsored by Business Strategy Network, Tillinghast-Towers Perrin, Weil Gotshal and Manges, and A.M. Best.
